text:
maria: quick share — did a focused A100 vs H100 end-to-end SLA fitment sweep for mosaic-7b and ggml-13b (q4_0/q8x4) across us-central and eu-west1. Prefill + decode p50/p99, tokens/sec, and $/1M tokens. small write-up below.

bench-bot: run finished — 6 configs, 48 trials, kv-cache cold/cached, fanout=1/2, seq_len=256. artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/2965432100/

alex: nice. top-line numbers? :eyes:

maria: TL;DR — H100 wins latency and throughput consistently for decode-heavy single-shard setups. A100 shows worse decode p50 and often falls back to non-fused kernels at higher seq lengths, which spikes prefill. Cost/$ tradeoffs depend on regional GPU price delta and slot efficiency.

sam: concrete numbers please — any $/1M tokens?

maria: yep. mosaic-7b q8x4 (single-stream synth chat, seq=256, kv-warm):
- H100: decode p50 ~18ms/token, p99 ~85ms/token, tokens/sec ~240, $/1M tokens ~2.10 (us-central)
- A100: decode p50 ~32ms/token, p99 ~160ms/token, tokens/sec ~140, $/1M tokens ~3.40 (us-central)
- EU-west1 GPU premium +12% -> H100 $/1M ~2.35, A100 ~3.80 (ballpark)

devon: surprising A100 so much worse on decode. what about prefill?

maria: prefill is where A100 gets hit harder because our runtime fell back on non-fused kernels for cross-attention matmul in some cases (seq>128, kv-fanout>1). numbers (mosaic-7b, same config):
- H100 prefill p50 ~110ms, p99 ~420ms
- A100 prefill p50 ~190ms, p99 ~950ms
Cold starts (kv-miss) amplify p99.

alex: can you paste the kernel trace that shows the fallthrough?

maria: sure — snippet from runtime logs (relevant lines):
```
kernel_select: fused_flash_attn_v2 -> OK on H100
kernel_select: matmul_cuBLAS_fallback (non-fused) on A100 for layer 10..15 (seq>128)
kv_cache: warm_hit_rate=0.78 for this workload
```

sam: so runtime decision is the key lever. did you force any quantization differences? q4_0 vs q8x4?

maria: tested both. q8x4 on mosaic-7b gave slightly better tokens/sec (H100 260 vs A100 150) but cost per 1M tokens differences narrowed because q8x4 increases memory pressure -> more frequent kernel fallbacks on A100 for higher seq. ggml-13b q4_0 showed ~0.8% perplexity regression on our open-eval slice vs fp16 baseline (small but visible).

devon: any region-specific capacity notes? fanout or pod sizing suggestions?

maria: yes — two notes:
1) For EU customers, prefer H100 reserved pools for high-throughput chat workloads — slot efficiency matters more than raw GPU list price because A100 needs more replication to hit latency SLOs.
2) For mixed QPS (multi-tenant), pipeline fanout=2 reduced p99 by ~20% on H100 but increased cost per token by ~8% due to extra replication; on A100 fanout helped p99 a bit but didn't overcome the kernel fallthrough penalty.

alex: any actionable runtime knobs we should try before recommending Dedicated H100?

maria: runtime knobs to try:
- force fused kernels where possible (experimental)
- cap seq_len at 180 for A100-backed pools to avoid fallthrough
- enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for chat to reduce prefill frequency
- try q8x4 only on H100 until kernel coverage improves on A100

bench-bot: note appended: observed increased thermal throttling on older A100 SKU after 6h sustained decode at 85% util — throughput droop ~6%.

sam: thanks — useful. any quality regressions tied to q4_0 that would block canary?

maria: not blocking but raise flags: ggml-13b q4_0 perplexity +0.8% on our conversational eval subset; recommend an eval canary using 2k prompt set before rollout.

infra-bot: reminder — file infra ticket if we want to spin Dedicated H100 pools in eu-west1, include expected sustained tokens/sec and target p99 latency.

devon: I'll draft the ticket with sizing estimates (using maria's tokens/sec numbers) and route to procurement. :+1:

maria: thanks. next step: I'll push the logs + kernel traces and a small runbook (how to cap seq_len and flip kernel flags) into the bench artifact bucket and schedule a 30m sync with capacity team tomorrow. :rocket:
